channel.title: The Cuenca Brief
channel.description:
The Cuenca Brief is a short, friendly news briefing for English speakers living in and around Cuenca, Ecuador. Three times a week: news from Cuenca and Azuay, the big stories from across Ecuador and the Andes, practical notices you can use, opportunities, culture and events. New episodes (Cuenca time): Sundays around 5 am, the week that was and the week ahead; Tuesdays around 4 pm, the latest news for the trip home; Fridays around 6:30 am, a catch-up on the week's news and your weekend preview for the morning commute. Every episode lists its sources in the notes.
Written with AI assistance and narrated by an AI voice. Produced by GRAC Labs. For advertising, message us on WhatsApp at +593 99 535 8888 (https://wa.me/593995358888) or email graclabs.ec@gmail.com.

item.title: Sunday, November 22: Mazar gets a brief reprieve
item.description:
The Mazar reservoir recovered slightly after the government took big industries off the power grid until Sunday midnight, while swollen rivers cut off communities in Chaucha and Molleturo and El Niño's national toll passed 100,000 people affected. Plus Peru's earthquake, Bolivia and Chile back at the table, and the week ahead: university registration, the November 25 marches, The Nutcracker, and what to know before the November 29 local elections.

In this episode:
Mazar recovers slightly after large industries go off-grid until Sunday midnight
Rivers destroy bridges in Chaucha and Molleturo; downpour floods northern Cuenca
New Hospital Municipal de Baños offers free specialist consultations
Noboa in Cuenca; mayoral and prefect debates at Teatro Pumapungo
Deportivo Cuenca loses 2–0 in Ambato; La Tri beats Bolivia 2–0
El Niño: at least 20 dead and nearly 105,000 affected nationwide; floods in Galápagos
Hegseth meets Noboa in Quito; Ecuadorian fishermen sue the US government
Aeroregional suspends Quito–Santa Rosa flights after a runway excursion
BIESS home loans for Ecuadorians abroad
Magnitude 6.7 earthquake in central Peru; Bolivia and Chile resume talks; Chile's economy shrinks; national strike in Colombia
Week ahead: Registro Nacional, education congress, November 25 marches, The Nutcracker, exhibitions, Deportivo Cuenca vs. Manta
Inamhi rain warning, election-day checklist, dry law, and the ECU 911 app for foreigners

item.title: Friday, November 20: Rivers cut off Chaucha and Molleturo
item.description:
Swollen rivers have damaged bridges and isolated communities in Chaucha and Molleturo, while heavy rain flooded northern Cuenca and big industries stay off the power grid until Sunday night as Mazar keeps falling. Plus the US defense secretary's meeting with President Noboa, and a weekend of indie music, birds, dance and Deportivo Cuenca on the road.

In this episode:
Rising rivers damage bridges and isolate communities in Chaucha and Molleturo
Thursday downpour floods streets in northern Cuenca
Large industries off the grid until Sunday midnight; diesel rationing reported
Noboa in Cuenca: farm equipment, water projects for Gualaceo and Sígsig, renovated Jefferson Pérez track
Cuenca mayor and Azuay prefect debates ahead of the November 29 elections
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth meets Noboa in Quito
Non-recoverable rest day across Ecuador for the Loja arts festival
Magnitude 6.7 earthquake in central Peru
Weekend: Guambra Sound at Teatro Pumapungo, bird expo, Cuerpos Elementales dance festival, Colibrí exhibition
Deportivo Cuenca visits Técnico Universitario in Ambato
Inamhi rain advisory, election silence and dry-law dates

(00:00) Headlines

item.content:encoded:
Swollen rivers have damaged bridges and isolated communities in Chaucha and Molleturo, while heavy rain flooded northern Cuenca and big industries stay off the power grid until Sunday night as Mazar keeps falling. Plus the US defense secretary's meeting with President Noboa, and a weekend of indie music, birds, dance and Deportivo Cuenca on the road.

In this episode:
Rising rivers damage bridges and isolate communities in Chaucha and Molleturo
Thursday downpour floods streets in northern Cuenca
Large industries off the grid until Sunday midnight; diesel rationing reported
Noboa in Cuenca: farm equipment, water projects for Gualaceo and Sígsig, renovated Jefferson Pérez track
Cuenca mayor and Azuay prefect debates ahead of the November 29 elections
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth meets Noboa in Quito
Non-recoverable rest day across Ecuador for the Loja arts festival
Magnitude 6.7 earthquake in central Peru
Weekend: Guambra Sound at Teatro Pumapungo, bird expo, Cuerpos Elementales dance festival, Colibrí exhibition
Deportivo Cuenca visits Técnico Universitario in Ambato
Inamhi rain advisory, election silence and dry-law dates

item.title: Tuesday, November 17: Mazar reservoir falls again
item.description:
The Mazar reservoir behind the Paute hydro complex is dropping again and stopped generating this morning, while Cuenca's mayoral and prefect candidates debate this Friday ahead of the November 29 local elections. Plus early bonus and pension payments, Colombia's investment push, and a week of salsa, symphonic concerts and a bird expo in Cuenca.

In this episode:
Mazar reservoir drops toward its critical level; turbines stop generating
Debates for Cuenca mayor and Azuay prefect on Friday, November 20, at Teatro Pumapungo
Partial lane closure on the Cuenca–Azogues highway for the Gapal interchange
Noboa repeats plan for a new airport at Taura to serve Azuay and El Oro
El Niño red alert: heavy rain tonight in seven coastal and western provinces
Christmas bonus and IESS pensions paid early; CyberDay runs through Wednesday
Mining exports up a third in the first nine months
Colombia announces nearly 26 billion dollars in planned investment
Ecuador vs. Bolivia tonight; concerts, salsa, bird expo and Guitar Raymi in Cuenca
Weather, a water cut, election-day dry law and the November 25 marches

item.title: Premiere: Welcome to The Cuenca Brief
item.description:
The Cuenca Brief is a short, friendly news briefing for English speakers living in and around Cuenca, Ecuador: news from Cuenca and Azuay, the big stories from across Ecuador and the Andes, practical notices you can use, opportunities, science and technology, culture, events and a little sports.

When new episodes arrive (Cuenca time, UTC−5):
Sundays around 5:00 am: the week that was and the week ahead (up to 15 minutes)
Tuesdays around 4:00 pm: the latest news, for the trip home (up to 10 minutes)
Fridays around 6:30 am: a catch-up on the week's news and your weekend preview, for the morning commute (up to 10 minutes)

First regular episode: Tuesday, November 17, 2026, around 4:00 pm. Sources for every story are listed in each episode's notes.
